name: Warren Conservation Park
reason: NPWS SA visitor page: free entry, open daily, three walking trails including a Heysen Trail section through stringybark woodland; a named-walk conservation park.

name: Bundaleer Forest
reason: Flinders Ranges and Outback tourism page (Bundaleer Reservoir Reserve): open daily, loop walking trail, kayaking, fishing, picnics, a day out from Clare. Keep as Bundaleer Reservoir Reserve/Forest, one place (the museum also names Bundaleer Forest).

name: Louden Brae School
reason: For: tourism-board listing of a restored 1905 one-teacher schoolhouse, famed as R.M. Williams' school. Against: single source, a stone building with a short visit, and the page gives no open-to-public detail (directions via the visitor outlet), so interior access is unconfirmed.

name: Diggers Walk Belalie Creek
reason: Tourism-board page: heritage creek-side trail built by WWI veterans, with interpretive displays on local WWI stories and Sir Hubert Wilkins, picnic/BBQ spots. Free open walk, half an hour or more.

name: Jamestown Mural Walk and Outdoor Gallery
reason: Tourism-board page: self-guided walk past heritage-building murals plus a permanent Outdoor Gallery of mural-festival works on Ayr Street, on display year-round (the festival is only how they were made).

name: Jamestown Railway Station Museum
reason: Tourism-board page: local-history museum in the 1885 railway station with an 1870s carriage, early three-wheeled car, Both Brothers medical equipment, and R.M. Williams and Farmers Union links. Opening days limited; a museum a guide names.

name: R.M. Williams Story (Jamestown)
reason: For: tourism-board listing of an outdoor interpretive display on the R.M. Williams brand founder, born near Jamestown, in Robinson Park (free, always accessible). Against: single source, an outdoor panel display likely 15 minutes, close in theme to the Louden Brae School and the museum's R.M. Williams exhibit.

name: Terowie
reason: SMH Traveller guide lists Terowie Historic Walk (35-39 buildings, ~2 hours), Arid Lands Botanic Garden, and a heritage main street; search results also name five museums and the MacArthur 'I shall return' plaque at the station; one of SA's seven historic towns. Two guide sources, a town draw in its own right. (Flinders and Outback region page was not confirmed to name it.)

name: Map the Miner
reason: Barossa tourism board lists MAP the Miner under Things to do > Heritage & landmarks; a 7 m bronze Cornish-miner statue on the Thiele Highway at Kapunda with picnic area and lookout, a named roadside Big Thing icon. Short stop, but quirky icons are keeps per COVERAGE.
